questions: Is the cost of swapping P_i and P_{i+1} always exactly i, regardless of the values being swapped, or does it depend on the values?
If multiple sequences of swaps achieve the sorted order with the same minimum total cost, does the answer require choosing any particular sequence, or just the minimum cost?
Does 'ascending order' mean strictly increasing from left to right, i.e., P_1 < P_2 < ... < P_N?
Is the cost additive per swap, i.e., total cost = sum of i for each swap performed?
Can we perform swaps in any order, and is the goal to minimize the sum of costs, not the number of swaps?
If N=2 and P is already sorted, is the cost 0?
Are there any constraints on the number of operations or time complexity for computing the answer?
Does the cost i refer to the position before the swap or after the swap, if indices shift due to previous swaps?
